name: Izon
sweep_summary: Izon (izon1238) is not in the catalog. The single title-match item, Efere 1981 'Pitch accent in the Bumo and Nembe dialects of Ijo', is a BA long essay from the University of Port Harcourt (Glottolog 41521; Bumo = Izon, Nembe = Southeast Ijo); it is about accent placement in this language but no copy exists online, and it is presumably superseded by Efere's 1994 thesis / 2001 UBC Working Papers monograph 'The pitch system of the Bumo dialect of Izon' (pp. 115-259), which I located bibliographically (Glottolog 32627/19432/19438) but could not fetch: every UBC host serves a browser-verification page, and Wayback, Google Books, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were offline or over quota. Crossref located Williamson 1988 'Tone and Accent in Ịjọ' (Foris, DOI 10.1515/9783110874266.253), paywalled behind a De Gruyter robot check, and the Ijaw-languages Wikipedia bibliography lists Williamson 1978 'From tone to pitch-accent: the case of Ịjọ' (Kiabàrà). No first-hand stress/accent statement was read; all evidence points to Izon being described as a pitch-accent (restricted tone) system, but that is inferred from titles only. Highest acquisition priorities: Efere 2001 (UBCWPL 4) and Williamson 1988. Saved:, glottolog_izon1238_refs.bib, }.
